# Testing {#sec-testing}

This chapter describes how AEE is verified.

## Unit tests

The SQF physics models are mirrored in Python and validated with `unittest`.
The suites cover every module: ballistics, thermal
(air density, WBGT, heat index, wind chill), mobility (SAE J1349 power,
slip traction, Nash cascade, NRMM, compass), physiology (hypoxia TUC, UV),
radio (Friis, ITU-R P.531), environmental (Q10 CBRN, Rothermel, Stefan),
and atmos (LWC icing, CAPE, EDR, WMO trend). Each test covers reference
values, edge cases (zero, extremes, clamp bounds), and monotonicity.

The MGRS and positioning work adds four suites. `test_mgrs` covers the
letter-table round trip. `test_geolocation` runs the real anchor builder
against its Python mirror for each world. `test_geo_positioning` covers the
consistency evaluator and the anchor contract. `test_gnss` covers the
error-ellipse, fix-state and datalink kernels. Each suite runs the real SQF
kernel through the `sqf_lite` harness where the kernel is pure.
The wildlife ecology kernels add two suites: `test_wildlife_ecology` and
`test_wildlife`. They run the real SQF kernels through the `sqf_lite`
harness with fixtures, and they pin the corpus to a fresh render. Each pure
kernel has a mutation proof: one edit makes exactly one test fail, then the
restore makes it pass.

The single-command runner executes every suite plus the physics validation
harness:

```bash
python3 tools/run_tests.py            # full sweep
python3 tools/run_tests.py --fast     # unit suites only
```

The unit tests run in the pre-commit hook, so a formula regression cannot
be committed.

## Server installation

The test needs an Arma 3 dedicated server installation. It is not bundled
with the repository. The dedicated server is free to download:

```bash
steamcmd +login anonymous +force_install_dir <path> +app_update 233780 validate
```

Point the test at that installation with the `ARMA3_SERVER_ROOT`
environment variable. Alternatively, copy or install the server into
`tests/docker/server` (the default location). The script checks for the
`arma3server_x64` binary and stops with instructions if it is missing.

The container mounts the server directory read-write. The server writes
its profile state to a tmpfs, so no root-owned files appear in the
repository.

## Headless dedicated-server test

The primary verification runs the mod on an Arma 3 dedicated server in
Docker. It uses the brettmayson/arma3server image. The test mission
`aee_test.Stratis` runs ten phases:

| Phase | Checks |
|---|---|
| 1 | Settings registered |
| 2 | Functions compiled and resolvable |
| 3 | Core state in physical ranges |
| 4 | Compat gating (no ACE3) |
| 5 | Determinism (temperature delta over 5 s) |
| 6 | Module coverage (state surface of every subsystem, 45 variables) |
| 7 | AI-unit dependent functions |
| 8 | Koppen classifier (17 biome codes) |
| 9 | Edge cases (boundary positions, nil/garbage inputs, extreme values, rapid state changes) |
| 10 | Performance gate (core functions within per-call budget: 1 ms on-demand, 5 ms for the 5 s update loop) |

```bash
tools/docker_test.sh
```

The script builds the mod, assembles `@aee`, downloads CBA if needed, runs
the server, captures the RPT output, and verifies the phase results.

## Concurrent and isolated runs

Every run uses a unique Docker compose project, so two runs never capture the
same container. A single run keeps the historical log path
`tests/docker/run.log` and port 2302.

For several runs at once, add `--isolate`. Each run then gets a unique run
directory under `tests/docker/runs/<id>/` and a free game-port block.

```bash
tools/docker_test.sh --isolate          # run.log moves to runs/<id>/
tools/docker_test.sh --run-id suite-a --isolate
```

The `--parallel` mode runs several suite modes at once and aggregates one
verdict. The parent builds once. Each child then skips the build and reuses
the assembled `@aee`.

```bash
tools/docker_test.sh --parallel                        # default maps
tools/docker_test.sh --parallel --jobs "default maps hosts"
tools/docker_test.sh --parallel default default        # two suites at once
tools/docker_test.sh --parallel maps:Tanoa maps:Enoch  # two worlds at once
```

A `maps` job may name one or more rotation worlds after a colon. Each named
world then runs as its own isolated job, so the rotation is split across
concurrent containers. A filter that names no runnable world fails the run.

The parent prints one PASS or FAIL line per job and one combined verdict. A
non-zero verdict fails the run. The derivation lives in
`tools/docker_run_isolation.py` and is unit-tested by
`tools/tests/test_docker_isolation.py`.

Environment overrides: `AEE_RUN_ID`, `AEE_RUN_DIR`, `AEE_GAME_PORT`,
`AEE_PROFILE`, `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`, `AEE_PORT_SLOT`, `AEE_SKIP_BUILD` and
`AEE_PARALLEL_JOBS`.

### Ecology probes

The wildlife ecology layer adds four probes. Each drives a pure kernel with
fixtures, or a kernel that reads the terrain only. No probe claims a rendered
pixel or a played sample. The `init.sqf` owns the single `[AEE-TEST] DONE`
line, and each probe emits its own `[P10n] [PASS]` or `[P10n] [FAIL]` line.

| Probe | Checks |
|---|---|
| P102 | Environment sampler budget and re-queue, and the pure cache cap and age |
| P103 | Ecology cognition tick budget, the front re-queue and the client gate |
| P104 | Call emit and receive semantics, and the heard-call bus |
| P105 | Sound emission schedule: dawn peak, mid-day lull, Dolbear duty cycle |

## Engine mass census

The engine config `mass` and `getMass` are engine tuning values, never a
real-world mass (`data/vehicle/SCHEMA.md`). A `mass` override must therefore
be a calibrated scale of a held real mass, so the engine's own mass is
measured first. Phase 72, the probe `aee_p72_mass_probe.sqf`, spawns one
instance of every class in `data/vehicle/class_bindings.json`, reads
`getMass` and deletes the instance. It measures only and applies nothing.
Each class emits one line:

```
[P72] MASS <class> config=<n> live=<n>
```

Run the census, then build the calibration:

```bash
tools/docker_test.sh                                  # writes tests/docker/run.log
python3 tools/validation/build_mass_calibration.py --log tests/docker/run.log
```

The tool writes `data/physics/mass_calibration.json`. It fails closed when
the log is absent or misses a bound class. The tool writes `approved: false`:
the operator approves the calibration, and the approval records the approver
and the date. The validator `tools/validation/validate_mass_calibration.py`
gates the written artefact; an absent artefact is a legal state.

When the calibration is approved, `tools/validation/gen_physics_config.py`
derives one mass per bound class as `real_analogue_mass_kg / fit.scale` and
emits it into the same `CfgVehicles` block as `maxSpeed`. The generator refuses
an unapproved calibration and a class with no held mass or no resolved parent.

## Baseline comparison

Run once without the mod to compare mission boot and engine weather:

```bash
tools/docker_test.sh --baseline
```

The phases fail in the baseline because no AEE mod is loaded. That is the
expected reference.

## Map rotation

The `--maps` mode runs the mission on several worlds and asserts each
resolved Koppen biome is PLAUSIBLE for the map's latitude. The latitude is
a fact read from the map's own `CfgWorlds` config (`abs` of the declared
value: BIS stores the sign inverted, and the Koppen band is symmetric).
There is no expected biome per map: the mode calls
`tools/validation/validate_biome_plausible.py <latitude> <biome>` and
passes when the validator accepts the band (ADR-002).

```bash
tools/docker_test.sh --maps
```

| World (CfgWorlds class) | Latitude | Required Workshop mod |
|---|---|---|
| Stratis | 35.097 | vanilla |
| Tanoa | 17.698 | vanilla (Apex) |
| Enoch | 54 | vanilla (Contact) |
| NorthTakistan | 17.698 | 2829330653, 583496184 (CUP Terrains Core) |
| kunduz_valley | 36.72 | 3078351739, 583496184 (CUP Terrains Core) |
| Mountains_ACR | 34 | 583544987 (CUP Terrains Maps), 583496184 |
| oski_corran | 56.702 | 2214384530 |

Before the rotation, `--maps` checks each map's required Workshop
directories under the local library. A missing dependency prints a
`MISSING` line, skips that map, and the run still exits 0. The library
root defaults to
`/ext/SteamLibrary/steamapps/workshop/content/107410` and can be
overridden with `AEE_WORKSHOP_DIR`. Each required Workshop item is bind
mounted inside the mods folder for the run; the mount is writable because
Arma's mod scanner resolves a read-only `:ro` bind mount as an empty mod.

## Host-mod compatibility

The `--hosts` mode loads each supported host mod with AEE and asserts the
compat integration produces state. Host mods are not committed to the
repository; download them from the Steam Workshop and extract them into
`tests/docker/mods/`:

| Host | Workshop folder | Workshop item |
|---|---|---|
| ACE3 | `tests/docker/mods/@ace` | 463939057 |
| ACRE2 | `tests/docker/mods/@acre2` | 751965892 |
| TFAR | `tests/docker/mods/@tfar` | 894678801 |
| KAT Advanced Medical | `tests/docker/mods/@kat_adv_medical` | 2020940806 |
| ACM | `tests/docker/mods/@acm` | 333310405 |

```bash
tools/docker_test.sh --hosts
```

The mode reports a PASS or FAIL per host. Missing mods are listed instead
of run.

ACM ships uppercase PBO filenames. The Arma Linux server canonicalises
them to lowercase internally and then cannot open the uppercase file on a
case-sensitive filesystem. The harness creates lowercase symlink aliases
for the ACM PBOs before the host test, so ACM loads correctly on Linux.

## Visual verification

::: {.callout-warning}
## Client required for pixels

The dedicated server has no renderer, so visual effects cannot be
verified headless.
:::

The dedicated server has no renderer. Visual effects (heat shimmer, HUD,
particles, sound) are verified at the state-variable level in phase 6 and
phase 7. Pixel-level visual QA needs a licensed game client.

## Agent-verifiable versus operator-only

A machine proves some results. Only a game client proves others. This
section states the boundary.

Agent-verifiable (a machine proves it):

- The pure kernels run through `tools/tests/sqf_lite.py`.
- The source contracts on the renderers, the force hooks, the gate kernel
  and the registry ownership.
- The Python validators.
- The HEMTT build and the pedantic check.
- The headless dedicated-server phases in `tools/docker_test.sh`.
- The nightly headless run on the self-hosted runner.
- The perception kernel, the deviation flags and the module-health report
  (Docker probe P100).
- The consistency evaluator against an agreeing and a ground-chain
  disagreeing fixture (Docker probe P101).

Operator-only (only a game client proves it):

- The starfield, aurora, Milky Way and meteor pixels.
- The NVG overlay clipping, fades and per-tier washout.
- The base grade and the felt sharpening.
- The felt eye adaptation and the perception overlay look.
- The alt-tab recovery and the advanced-optic recovery.
- The CBA settings menu. Open Addon Options: `AEE Experimental > Fusion`
  shows the four thermal-fusion knobs, `AEE HUD > Displays` shows the four
  on-screen display toggles, and `AEE Debug > <component>` shows the
  diagnostic switches. Every per-module `logDebug` switch sits under
  `AEE Debug`. Only the operator confirms the menu renders as intended.

## Observability and consistency

Two Docker probes verify the observability surface headless. Both are pure
kernel probes and run on the dedicated server, so neither needs a local
player.

- **P100 - perception and module health.** Seeds a fixture value map, calls
  `perceptionSample` and `perceptionDetectDeviation`, and checks the schema
  length, the clean flags, the discolouration flag, the blindness flag and
  the module-health report. Prints `[P100] [PASS]` or `[P100] [FAIL]`.
- **P101 - consistency.** Loads the invariant table, seeds an agreeing map
  and a ground-chain disagreeing map, calls `evaluateConsistency`, and checks
  that the disagreeing map raises exactly the expected rows and names the two
  scalar producers that diverge. Prints `[P101] [PASS]` or `[P101] [FAIL]`.

The harness fails when either tag is missing from `tests/docker/run.log`.
The two probes move the perception state, the deviation flags, the
module-health report and the consistency verdict onto the agent-verifiable
list. The felt eye adaptation and the perception overlay pixels stay
operator-only.
